Built-in adapters share three conceptual operations: preflight, invoke, and
extract the final response. Model catalogs are never discovered automatically;
configured model names are the reproducible source of truth.

## OpenCode

ForgeCycle uses `opencode run --standalone`, attaches the turn manifest with `--file`, selects
the candidate's model and effort variant together as `--model
provider/model#variant` (OpenCode 2 removed the `--variant` flag), and requests
JSON events. The variant is the candidate's `native_effort` when set, otherwise
its `effort`; a configured model that already contains `#` is passed unchanged. The final
text event becomes the candidate handoff. Read-only mode selects OpenCode's plan
agent, workspace-write uses its configured permission policy, and unrestricted
mode adds `--auto`. OpenCode does not expose a native filesystem boundary flag;
use its permission configuration when a hard workspace boundary is required.

`--standalone` is always passed and cannot be turned off. It runs the turn on
a private OpenCode server, a child of the `opencode` process ForgeCycle
starts, instead of OpenCode's shared background service. When a turn times
out or is interrupted, stopping `opencode` also stops that server and the
tools it runs, and no turn depends on the version or state of a service
started earlier. Each turn takes a few seconds longer to start. A job an
agent detaches on purpose (`nohup … &`, a browser daemon) still outlives the
server; the sweep of the worktree after each turn stops it there (see
[Observability](/documentation/guides/observability/)).

Development baseline: OpenCode 2.1.4. `doctor` and `task run` exit 65 when
`opencode run --help` does not list `--standalone`, before any turn starts;
update OpenCode with `opencode upgrade`. OpenCode 1.x is not supported
because it does not accept `model#variant`. `doctor` warns when the version
is outside the configured tested pattern (2.1 or later) and still attempts
compatibility. `doctor --ping`
invokes each configured candidate through the same adapter invocation as a real
read-only turn, so it also proves the model and effort flags are accepted.

## Codex CLI

ForgeCycle uses `codex exec --json`, `--model`,
`model_reasoning_effort` (the candidate's `native_effort` when set, otherwise its
`effort`), `-C`, and `--output-last-message`. Permission levels map
to native sandbox flags; unrestricted mode uses Codex's explicit approval/sandbox
bypass option.

Development baseline: codex-cli 0.163.0.

## Claude Code CLI

ForgeCycle uses `claude -p --output-format json`, passes the turn manifest on
standard input, and extracts the `result` field. It selects the configured model
with `--model` and effort with `--effort`. A candidate's `native_effort` overrides
its normalized effort. Read-only uses `plan`, workspace-write uses `auto`, and
unrestricted uses `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Claude's auto mode reviews
tool calls, but it does not create a hard filesystem boundary; configure Claude
Code sandboxing if the run needs one. ForgeCycle disables session persistence so
each invocation relies on its manifest rather than a saved Claude session.

Development baseline: Claude Code 2.1.289.

## Antigravity CLI

The supported headless command is `agy`, not the Antigravity IDE launcher.
ForgeCycle uses print mode with JSON output, model, effort, permission mode, and a
large explicit `--print-timeout`. The prompt is attached to the flag
(`--print=<prompt>`): agy rejects a bare `--print` followed by another flag and
never reads the prompt from stdin in print mode. Timeout warnings and partial
success responses are normalized to `timeout` even when `agy` exits zero.
Read-only uses plan mode, workspace-write uses accept-edits, and unrestricted also
adds `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. `--effort` is the candidate's
`native_effort` when set, otherwise its `effort`.

Development baseline: agy 1.4.2; the attached-prompt requirement was verified
against 1.2.3.

## Normalized failures

Adapters classify `protocol_error`, `authentication_error`, `quota_exhausted`,
`rate_limited`, `unavailable`, `timeout`, `invocation_error`, and `interrupted`.
Classification reads stderr and also the structured provider error a CLI prints
on stdout. opencode reports `{"type":"error","error":{"data":{"statusCode":429,…}}}`
and codex reports `{"type":"turn.failed","error":{"message":…}}`, both with an
empty stderr. Claude reports `is_error` together with the `result` text. Only
these top-level error envelopes are read; model text nested in other events is
never classified.

Authentication failure skips remaining candidates using the same adapter for
that turn. Events include a normalized `retryable=true|false` property and are
recorded without raw prompts or provider output. Protocol, rate-limit,
availability, timeout, and generic invocation failures are retryable.
Authentication, interruption, and quota exhaustion are not. On a
`timeout_seconds` timeout, or when ForgeCycle is interrupted, the
CLI gets SIGTERM so it can end its session, then SIGKILL after 10 seconds.

`quota_exhausted` covers usage limits that will not recover within a retry
sweep ("You've hit your usage limit", "Weekly/Monthly Limit Exhausted", agy's
"Individual quota reached", insufficient credits). ForgeCycle parses a reset
time from the message: an absolute `reset at 2026-10-07 19:17:39` (local time
unless a zone is given), a clock time `try again at 2:52 AM`, or a relative
`try again in 20 minutes`, `try again in 1 hour 30 minutes`, or compact
`Resets in 23h3m39s`.
The candidate is then put on a persistent cooldown in
`.forgecycle/adapter-cooldowns.json` until that time. When no future reset
time is found, the cooldown lasts `quota_cooldown_seconds` (default 3600).
Every run in the repository skips a cooled-down candidate, recording
`skipped, quota cooldown until …` in its failure list and `events.log`.

Version-one adapters are internal and intentionally not a public plugin API.
